verses.1: And the people cried out loudly, and their women also cried out loudly to their Jewish brothers.
verses.2: And there are those who say, “Our sons and daughters, we are many. We will be taken away as slaves, and we will be eaten.”
verses.3: And there are those who say that our vineyards and gardens, and our children, will be taken away from us in the evening, and we will be deprived of our crops.
verses.4: And there are those who say to our king, “Gold is enough for the expenses of our kings and our vineyards.”
verses.5: And now, we are binding our brothers with ropes. We bind their children as well. And behold, we are binding our own children and daughters to serve others. Some of our daughters are also bound and cannot escape. Our vineyards belong to others.
verses.6: I was extremely upset when I heard their cries and these words.
verses.7: And my heart became king over me. I gathered together the men and women, and said to them, “One man among you is a woman. So I will give them a great honor.”
verses.8: And she said to them, “We have purchased our Jewish brothers who are being sold to other nations. So, you too will sell your brothers to us. They will be sold to us, and we will take possession of them. But they couldn’t find any reason for this.”
verses.9: And he said, “It is not good what you are doing. Do not go away from our God’s presence, lest you be destroyed by the nations that hate us.”
verses.10: And I, my brothers and my sons, have also given them gold and silver in exchange for them. Please leave this worthless thing behind.
verses.11: Please give them back today what they lost: their gardens, their vineyards, and their homes. Also, give them back the money, the goods, and the possessions that you have taken from them.
verses.12: And they said, “Let them be put back in their places. No one will be asked to do anything else. As you say, I will call upon the priests and make them carry out this order.”
verses.13: I too was a young girl, and I said, “May God make this man become a youth who will not refuse to do this. And so, he will be young and pure.” All the people agreed with this, and they praised Jehovah. The people did as he commanded them.
verses.14: Also from the day when I was commanded to become “fossil” in the land of Judah, from the age of forty to the age of fifty-two. During those years, I and my brothers were nothing but “fossil” remains. I never ate anything at all.
verses.15: And the first rulers who came before me took control over the people. They took from them bread and wine, along with forty silver coins. Their daughters also ruled over the people. But I did not do this out of fear of God.
verses.16: And even during this hot summer, I continued to work hard. I didn’t stop working at all. All my boys were gathered there, working together on the work.
verses.17: And the Jews and the scribes were one hundred and fifty men. They came to us from the nations around us, who were located on our surrounding lands.
verses.18: And on that day, six hundred sheep and goats were slaughtered for me. In twelve days, in every direction, many people were given bread to eat. But I did not ask for any more bread, because the work was too heavy for this people.
verses.19: May God remember me for all the good I’ve done for this people.
